## Purpose and selected layouts

Calculate terminal-referenced transmission, reflection and fields for the
selected through-CPW coupled to a short–open meander resonator. Compare two
authored source variants while retaining the resonator and 17 airbridges:

- Lumped: launchers with internal nonmetal Signal–Ground support sheets.
- Wave: no launchers; constant-width CPW ends at exterior cuts.

The reproducible public source pair is being integrated with this notebook
suite, not presented here as already published.
[View the source layouts](../../public-pdk-examples/test-components.md#driven-terminal-lumped-and-wave-port-comparison).

## Model and excitation choices

Preserve Signal, Ground, substrate, bridge decks/posts and their physical
contact/Z relationships. Specify the vacuum region and exterior treatment.

Terminal is the solution kind; Lumped and Wave are port kinds. For Lumped
excitation, distinguish the internal support normal from its directed
Signal–Ground integration line. For Wave excitation, define the exterior
cross-section and reference conductors. In both cases retain port ordering,
impedance/normalization, renormalization and de-embedding intent.

Setup frequency controls adaptation; the sweep defines the returned response
samples. Mesh, pass controls and field retention govern numerical evidence.
Their concrete values live only in the corresponding notebook.

## Workflow

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Palace

A Palace driven comparison would need an explicitly stated excitation basis
and response convention. Shared layout does not turn it into HFSS Terminal
data or establish port-kind equivalence.

### AEDT

Use the separate [Lumped notebook](../../notebooks/ComponentSimulation/CpwMeanderAirbridge/aedt_hfss_driven_terminal_lumped.ipynb)
and [Wave notebook](../../notebooks/ComponentSimulation/CpwMeanderAirbridge/aedt_hfss_driven_terminal_wave.ipynb).
Construct the selected variant, inspect native Terminal assignments and
reference conductors, then perform adaptation and the requested sweep.
Resolve each returned run independently.

:::

## Expected outputs

Retain native solution type, port sheets/cut geometry, terminal references,
integration directions and material/contact readback. Return terminal S-data
and magnitude/phase plots with frequency, ordering and reference convention,
alongside adaptive and sweep history.

::: {.callout-note}
Touchstone reference impedance is not solved modal Wave-port characteristic
impedance. Keep those quantities separate. Matching resonator geometry does
not establish equivalent Lumped and Wave responses.
:::
